shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures rose for a third straight session on Friday, supported by a weaker yen and a rally in Tokyo equities, though the contract posted a weekly decline as oil prices fell.($1 = 156.9000 yen)($1 = 6.6969 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures rose for a third straight session on Friday, supported by a weaker yen and a rally in Tokyo equities, though the contract posted a weekly decline as oil prices fell.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
was up 2.3 yen, or 0.54%, at 430.2 yen ($2.74) per kg.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
fell 250 yuan, or 1.32%, to 18,670 yuan ($2,787.86) per metric ton.
The most active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) lost 320 yuan, or 2.14%, to 14,645 yuan per metric ton.
sank against its major peers in Asian trading on Friday, after a widely expected rate hike by the Bank of Japan failed to halt the currency's decline.
A weaker currency makes yen-denominated assets more affordable to overseas buyers.
Against that backdrop, the Nikkei (N.225) surged 1.7% to 65,221.53, topping the psychological 65,000 mark for the first time in more than a week.

Thai latex and cup lump prices have been relatively strong recently, with upstream processing plants holding low inventories and showing a strong willingness to restock, providing cost support for natural rubber, said analysts from broker Guangzhou Futures in a report.
Oil prices fell 2% on Friday, extending losses for a third straight session, as easing concerns over Saudi supply disruptions outweighed anxiety about a widening Middle East conflict.
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for December delivery (STFZ6) last traded at 235.3 US cents per kg, down 0.9% as of 0700 GMT.
